Quick follow-up while we've been using a local plugin that backports this exact `directory` param to `task` (shadow registration via opencode plugin API, stop-gap until this lands upstream): we hit a related Web UI gotcha that's worth documenting alongside this feature, since it surfaces precisely when the per-project subagent dispatch starts working as intended.

### Setup

After dispatching a subagent with `task({ directory: "<repo>/backend/api/v3", ... })`, the child session is correctly created with `directory=<repo>/backend/api/v3`. **TUI side everything works as expected** — `session_child_first` keybind navigates into the running child live, regardless of where TUI is anchored.

### Web UI behaviour

opencode Web UI renders a **per-project session list view** by filtering through `GET /session?directory=<X>`. Result:

| Web UI open in | Sees parent (`directory=<repo_root>`) | Sees child (`directory=<repo_root>/backend/api/v3`) live |
|---|---|---|
| `<repo_root>` | ✅ | ❌ (only after child finishes) |
| `<repo_root>/backend/api/v3` | ❌ | ✅ live |

After the child finishes the subtask-card click in the parent session opens it normally (different render path — direct ID lookup, not listing).

### Probe data confirming `directory` filter on `/session` listing

While a child session was live (parent's `directory=<repo_root>`, child's `directory=<repo_root>/backend/api/v3`):

```text
GET /session                                          → child NOT in listing (count=0)
GET /session?directory=<repo_root>                    → child NOT in listing (count=0)
GET /session?directory=<repo_root>/backend/api/v3     → child IS in listing (count=1) ✅

# But direct lookup by ID and parentID-traversal both work cross-instance:
GET /session/<child_id>                  → HTTP 200, identical JSON regardless of ?directory=
GET /session/<child_id>?directory=<any>  → HTTP 200, identical JSON
GET /session/<parent>/children           → child IS in array (no directory filter applied)
```

So the route-level layer is fine — direct GET and parent→children traversal don't filter by directory. The `/session` listing endpoint that Web UI consumes for its session list does.

### Why this matters here specifically

Once this feature ships, monorepo orchestrator workflows will routinely produce child sessions in subdirectories of the parent. Without a complementary tweak on the Web UI side, the live monitoring experience splits:

- **TUI users** — full visibility, child-session navigation works.
- **Web UI users** — have to open the target subproject in a second tab/window to see the child live; or wait for finish.

The workaround (open both projects in Web UI in parallel) is acceptable but worth being aware of when announcing this feature.

### Diff in child session metadata that drives the filter

The `/session` listing-side filter keys off two fields that differ between a parent-instance child and a target-instance child:

```diff
- "directory": "<repo_root>",
- "path": "",
+ "directory": "<repo_root>/backend/api/v3",
+ "path": "backend/api/v3",
```

Everything else (`projectID`, `parentID`, `agent`, `model`, `permission`, ...) is byte-for-byte identical between the two metadata shapes. So the routing is purely off `directory`.

### Suggestion (separate from the core feature, listing-side)

When the parent session has the listing open, surface its `children` regardless of their own `directory` — either by:

1. UI side: in addition to `/session?directory=<parent_dir>`, also call `/session/<parent_id>/children` (cross-instance, already works on the API) and merge.
2. Or API side: a `?include_children=true` flag on `/session?directory=<X>` that pulls in children of in-scope sessions regardless of their own directory.
